product_tiers.notes: GitHub provides a self‑serve OAuth app registration without a review step.

summary: GitHub offers a free, self‑serve OAuth app registration via the developer settings page; apps use the standard OAuth 2.0 flow and do not require a formal approval process for basic scopes.
verdict_note: Agent check: The developer portal is behind a login (https://github.com/settings/developers).

time.setup_notes: Registration requires a logged‑in GitHub account and filling out a short form; exact time varies per developer.

approval_wait.label: None for basic install · Marketplace: not published
approval_wait.notes: GitHub does not publish a wait time for OAuth app approval; basic apps are usable immediately after registration.

prerequisites.notes: A personal GitHub account is needed to access the developer settings page.
The registration page is behind a login screen.

steps.title: Log in to GitHub
steps.detail: Sign in to your GitHub account at https://github.com and ensure you have access to the developer settings page.

steps.title: Navigate to OAuth app registration
steps.detail: Visit https://github.com/settings/developers and click “New OAuth App”.

steps.title: Fill out app details
steps.detail: Enter the application name, homepage URL, description, and the Authorization callback URL (must be HTTPS except for localhost).

steps.title: Save the app
steps.detail: Click “Register application”. GitHub will display the Client ID and Client Secret needed for OAuth flows.

steps.title: Implement OAuth flow
steps.detail: Use the authorization endpoint https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize and token endpoint https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token in your application code.
